$comment: THE LIST CI RUNS, not a description of one (#396, stage 1).
scripts/run-checks.mjs iterates this file and ci.yml invokes that runner, so an entry
here IS an execution. A declared list CI did not iterate would be a second source of
truth and worse than the YAML it replaced: it would report a set nobody ran.
Each entry runs its PROOF first and its CHECKER second, in one process, because a
checker whose proof did not run is a checker nobody has watched fail. That ordering was
previously spelled out in six separate `pnpm <name>` scripts chaining `&&`; it is now a
property of the runner, so it cannot be forgotten on the seventh.
STAGE 1 covers only the six that already had the proof-first form. The other 45 checker
steps in ci.yml keep their own steps and pairing keeps parsing YAML for them.

checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR, NOT A SNAPSHOT. The derivation run reported 32 and a floor of 32 was a SCHEDULED FAILURE: this subject is the branch-protection required-context list, which is external config, so retiring one CI job drops it to 31 and the check refuses — reporting 'a green whose subject is under the floor' about a tree that is fine. What the floor needs to catch is an EMPTY result (the API answered with nothing), and 1 does that completely. Found by DEV3-lang.

checks.floorNote: ATTESTED AGAINST A BRANCH TREE, WHICH DOES NOT SURVIVE THE SQUASH — the same honest cost `eject-subjects-classified` records for its first anchor. `a9c8054a` is a commit on #1132's branch and becomes unreachable when that lands. It was the only option: the count BECOMES 8 because #1132 removes the `react-dom` entry, so no tree on main has ever held 8 and an attestation naming one would record a number false of the tree it names. 6 of the 45 shas in this file are already unreachable from main. Re-anchor at the next measurement rather than treating the dead sha as a defect. AND THE FLOOR ITSELF IS A KNOWN-WEAK FORM (#1131): 9 was the observed count, so it refused on the first legitimate removal it ever saw — the same scheduled failure `required-contexts` records above. checks.name: ladder-is-cumulative
checks.why: #788. assert-every-rung-is-witnessed:9 says the ladder being cumulative is "a real guarantee stated nowhere". It has two dependents that would both stay green if it stopped holding: rung-witnessing (a rung nothing removes is never shown severable) and #755's audit (eject-to-rung-1 treated as the maximal strip, so a subject static under it is static under every weaker target). This asserts the CONSEQUENCE both rely on — closure(requires, N) == the rungs at or below ordinal N — rather than the chain shape that currently produces it
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR. Its subject is the rung count, legitimately 1 in a rung-1 fork and 5 on main — and forks are exactly where severability is measured, so a floor at the observed 5 would refuse where this matters most. A floor of 1 catches the vacuity that matters: a manifest with no rungs.

checks.name: vocabulary-checker-dependency
checks.why: #779. assert-approval-vocabulary-agrees asks an INSTALLED langchain what interrupt_on expands to, and ci.yml puts that pip install in a different step, under a different working-directory, named for something else ("FastAPI backend tests"). Nothing connected them: rename, reorder or split the job and the checker exits 2 forever — correctly, loudly, permanently, which is what a recorded-but-unasserted dependency always fails into. #778 wrote the reason down; a record is not an assertion
checks.floorNote: The subject is the number of checker invocations paired with an install, and there is exactly one invocation, so this is 1 by construction rather than by measurement. A vanished invocation refuses at exit 2 before any subject is reported, so the floor's only job is to catch a run that reports a pairing count of zero while still claiming to have checked.

checks.name: census-survives-the-merge
checks.why: #145's silent half: two branches each adding one rung-owned file both freeze N+1 from a base of N, so git sees the same number on both sides, merges cleanly, and the merged tree holds N+2 declaring N+1. assert-census-fresh already catches exactly this and its SILENT case proves it — but it was invoked once, gated to pull_request, asking about a BRANCH merging into its base. Nobody asked it about two branches merging into each other, which is what a batch is. Measured: on such a merged tree classify.mjs, census.mjs and freeze-all.mjs all exit 0, so wiring those in closes nothing
checks.floorNote: NOT DERIVED YET, and a floor probably EXISTS. This check refuses on a non-merge HEAD, so the derivation run could not reach it. Derive it from a run on a MERGE COMMIT and replace this note. `floorPending` marks it so a later run can be told which entries to derive, and so a reader can tell this apart from a floor that can never exist.

checks.name: merge-keeps-registrations
checks.why: two branches appending to one registration list conflict, and taking either side wholesale drops the other's entry — for this very file that means a checker that never runs (#467)
checks.floorNote: NOT DERIVED YET, same gate: it refuses on a non-merge HEAD. A positive floor would be a guess about a run nobody has taken. Derive from a merge commit and replace this note. AND THE SUBJECT COUNT IS NOT FIXED AT FIVE — read this before deriving. `reportSubject` counts lists COMPARED, and since #1027 a list absent from all three trees is skipped before it reaches that count. So the number legitimately SHRINKS on a merge of trees that predate a list. A floor taken from a merge where every list happened to be present would be tripped later by a CORRECT skip, which is the scheduled failure this note exists to prevent. Derive it from the smallest count a legitimate merge can produce, not from a convenient one.

checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR, same reason. checks.name: eject-subjects-classified
checks.why: a subject count can be PRINTED rather than computed, and #741's floor cannot see it (#755). This gate is the cheap half: it asserts every registered checker has an eject classification. The measurement that produces them is `pnpm eject-audit`, ~5 minutes, on demand.
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR. Its subject is the registered-checker count, which is >= 1 by construction whenever checks.json is non-empty; the floor exists to catch a reading that enumerated nothing, not to bound the registry's size. THE OBSERVED SHA IS A PRE-SQUASH BRANCH COMMIT, DELIBERATELY. A brand-new check cannot cite a sha on main — this checker does not exist at b22774ec, so counting 48 there is impossible, and inventing a main sha to look durable would name a tree where the measurement could not have been taken. 325006a7 is this branch merged with main, which is a tree someone can check out and re-measure; it does not survive the squash, and that is the honest cost of a first anchor. Same trade as the census's `measuredAt` vs `base` (#755). AND THE RECORD IS DECORATIVE FOR THIS ENTRY (#811). `floorObserved` exists so a DERIVED number can be confirmed or falsified against the tree it came from. This floor is 1 — a vacuity floor, chosen rather than derived — so the sha confirms nothing about it. Having a `floorObserved` is not the same as having provenance, and this one is present because the gate requires it rather than because it carries information.

checks.name: format-writes
checks.why: `pnpm format` passing paths dropped --write, so prettier printed to stdout and left every file byte-identical while printing its normal banner — a repair that silently does nothing, which is worse than a missing one because the person running it stops looking. A commit was made on the strength of one such run (#816).
checks.floorNote: The subject is the enumerated INVOCATION FORMS in the checker, not a discovered set, so the floor is the list's length and moves only when someone adds or removes a form deliberately. It catches the vacuity that matters here: a checker that plants nothing and reports 0 forms verified would otherwise pass. ZERO MARGIN IS DELIBERATE AND PRICED: #791 permits floor == observed count only because floorObserved records the tree it was seen on, so a future bump is a reviewable edit against a checkout-able sha rather than a number someone raised to make a red go away.

checks.name: lifts-pointers-open
checks.why: a `lifts` pointer is validated for SHAPE by the registration gate and nothing checked that the issue it names is still OPEN — which is #824's own incident, where a pointer was cleared on the belief its issue had closed and it had not (#824). Reads BOTH `lifts` fields since #835: `checks.json`'s `unregistered[].lifts` and the census's `checkers[].lifts`, which is where every live pointer actually is.
checks.floorNote: NO FLOOR, AND THE DOMAIN IS NO LONGER EMPTY. Since #835 this reads both sources and examines three pointers, all naming #780; before that it read `checks.json` alone, where every entry is `lifts: null`, and passed green having examined ZERO. `floor: 0` still states that an empty domain is the right answer rather than a collapse — pointers are added and removed by ordinary work and there is no number this should be above, so a repo that has ruled every open question legitimately reads zero. What changed is that zero can no longer mean NOT LOOKING: an unreadable or unparseable source exits 2 instead of contributing a silent zero. The subject line reports the pointer count and is read from the files on every run rather than written here, because this number has already moved once.

checks.name: no-ascii-escapes
checks.why: a JSON serializer run with ensure_ascii rewrites every non-ASCII character as a \uXXXX escape, and the file still parses to the identical object — so this reached main in #821, turning 29 literal em-dashes into 41 escape occurrences and conflicting thirty lines of other people's prose for four branches. No instrument we own can see it: name comparison reads NAMES, prettier reads SYNTAX, and a parsed diff normalises both spellings to one string before comparing. All three pass by construction, for any input, which is why the guard has to read bytes. It asserts over the escape CLASS rather than the em-dash, because main's 41 occurrences all happened to be em-dashes and an em-dash-only rule would silently pass curly quotes and en-dashes next time.
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR, chosen rather than derived, and it may only ACCUSE. Its subject is the number of JSON strings read out of scripts/checks.json — 767 at the observed sha — and pinning the floor to that would be a threshold set to today, failing the moment a check is removed for a good reason. 100 catches the failure this floor exists for: a truncated or empty read reporting no violations because it examined nothing. It cannot clear anything, and no verdict rests on the value. THE OBSERVED SHA IS MAIN, NOT A BRANCH COMMIT, AND THE COUNT IS REPRODUCIBLE THERE. This checker does not exist at f4728d20, but its SUBJECT does: the count was taken by running this scanner over `git show f4728d20:scripts/checks.json`. So unlike a first anchor that must cite a pre-squash branch commit nobody can check out later, this one names a tree that survives and a measurement anyone can repeat.

checks.name: proofs-are-reachable
checks.why: a `*.selftest.mjs` that no route runs is indistinguishable from a deleted one — it sits in the tree, gets cited in review, and asserts nothing. Three were found that way at 110d547f, one of them named exactly once in the whole repository inside a `reason` STRING that claimed it did the work. assert-checkers-registered passes on that tree and is right to: its rule is about CHECKERS, all three of those were legitimately `unregistered`, and nothing in that rule mentions their SELFTESTS. So a green gate and three unreachable proofs coexisted with no contradiction until someone asked about reachability rather than registration. The predicate here is REACHABILITY, not runnable-by-`pnpm checks`: workflow-only PASSES, because whether those 34 should be registered is a decision per file that this must not pre-empt.
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR, chosen rather than derived, and it may only ACCUSE. The subject is the number of `scripts/*.selftest.mjs` on disk — 86 at the observed sha — and pinning the floor there would be a threshold set to today, failing the moment a proof is legitimately removed. 50 catches the failure this floor exists for: a readdir that returned a truncated set, or a glob that matched nothing, reporting no unreachable proofs because it examined almost none. It cannot clear anything. THE OBSERVED SHA IS MAIN AND THE COUNT IS REPRODUCIBLE THERE: this checker does not exist at 110d547f, but its SUBJECT does, and `git ls-tree -r --name-only 110d547f scripts/ | grep -c '.selftest.mjs$'` returns 86. So unlike a first anchor that must cite a pre-squash branch commit nobody can fetch later, this one names a tree that survives and a measurement anyone can repeat.

checks.why: the E2E approval-card budget was 30_000ms against a frame release at 38_590ms — upstream close plus the server's 30_000ms drain grace — so the deadline could not be met on an engine that waits for stream end, and five specs failed in one night reading as browser flakes (#675)
checks.floorNote: the five declared constants the relationship is built from; a drop means one was renamed or inlined, which the checker reports as a REFUSAL rather than a pass. THE SHA IS PRE-SQUASH AND SAYS SO: three of the five constants are introduced by this change, so no commit on main describes this subject yet and recording a main sha would be a field that reads as provenance and is not — the failure the external-subject guard in run-checks.mjs names. THIS ANCHOR IS EXPECTED TO BECOME UNREACHABLE, not merely at risk of it: the branch is deleted on squash-merge, after which this sha is in ZERO local refs by design. That is #852's shape and it is stated rather than left to be discovered. It stays recoverable from refs/pull/N/head, which keeps the branch tip and fetches over git protocol; replace it with the squash commit at the next measurement, when main will finally describe this subject.

checks.why: dev-all.sh printed the open-swe app and queue-agent URLs even in the branch that says it is skipping them, so the box advertised services that could not be running — a user spent an evening on an unresponsive port (#878)
checks.floorNote: the two rows whose service cannot be running when HAS_OPENSWE is 0. A drop means a row was renamed or removed, which the checker reports as a REFUSAL rather than a pass. THE SHA IS PRE-SQUASH AND SAYS SO: this checker is introduced by this change, so no commit on main describes its subject yet, and a main sha here would read as provenance and not be. It dies at every rebase and again at the squash — observed three times on #870 — and is recoverable from refs/pull/N/head. Replace it with the squash commit at the next measurement.

checks.name: worktree-inventory
checks.why: orphaned probe worktrees accumulate because nothing ties their lifetime to the branch they hold, and the two obvious repairs are both unsafe — a teardown does not fire on SIGKILL, and a prefix sweep deletes a concurrent peer's live probe. This REPORTS and removes nothing (#826, #873).
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR, NOT A SNAPSHOT. The subject is the worktree count on whatever machine runs it — 159 here, 1 on a CI runner — so any snapshot floor is a scheduled failure on a machine that is fine. What the floor must catch is an EMPTY inventory, which is what an unreadable `git worktree list` would produce if it were not a refusal, and 1 does that completely: every clone has at least its own checkout. The count below is provenance, not a bound, and is not re-takeable anywhere but the machine that took it.

checks.name: bot-silence-classified
checks.why: a bot that opened no PR is either SATURATED or STALLED and the output is identical — no new PR — so silence is read as health. The discriminator is capacity, open against `open-pull-requests-limit`, and it needs no run log, which is the thing GitHub does not expose (#810).
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR. The subject is the number of ecosystems declared in .github/dependabot.yml — 2 today — and a floor pinned to 2 would fail the day someone legitimately retires one. What must be caught is a config that parses to NOTHING, which would compare no capacity at all and pass; the checker refuses on that outcome and a floor of 1 is the second guard on the same hole. The count below is provenance and moves whenever an ecosystem is added or removed.

checks.name: doc-claims
checks.why: the rung docs, and the comments beside pinned versions, assert facts that were true when written and are never re-derived. #364's instance: nobody edited the doc, the code improved underneath it and the claim went false in place. #776 adds version constraints as a fourth kind — the only one of its three whose subject is a file this repo already reads.
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR, not a count. The subject sums the two kinds that enumerate their own claims — repo-relative paths and @version-claim markers — and a floor pinned to today's 83 would fail the day a doc legitimately drops a path. What must be caught is a run that examined NO claim: the corpus present and nothing checkable in it, which is the shape every vacuity failure here has taken. The count below is provenance and moves whenever a doc or a marker is added or removed.

checks.name: action-pin-comments
checks.why: a pin's version comment is the only human-readable statement of what its 40-hex sha is, and nothing resolved the two against each other. Dependabot preserves each line's comment while changing the sha, so a comment that was already stale stays stale: 50 of 82 named a version their sha was not, and two of five actions were wrong in EVERY pin, where a pins-agree-with-each-other check finds nothing

checks.name: git-subject-stances
checks.why: a script that asks git which files exist or changed is blind to a file a branch ADDS until it is committed — which is exactly when someone runs it. Patched three times independently (#209, #224, #856) before anyone gated the class; the stance may be "out-of-scope", it may not be silence (#899)
checks.floorNote: A FLOOR, NOT AN EQUALITY, and it protects against the classifier rather than against the repo. Membership is inferred by scanning source for git subcommand literals, so the failure mode that matters is the pattern silently matching FEWER scripts — which shrinks this gate's subject while it still reports PASS. Adding a git-subject script raises the count and trips nothing; losing one is the review moment. 14 measured, not inferred.

floorObserved.note: the BASE this was measured against, not the introducing commit — a commit cannot record its own sha, since amending to insert it changes it. 14 counts this base plus the checker itself, which is in its own population.

checks.subjectKindNote: DECLARED, not defaulted. The population unions tracked scripts with `--others --exclude-standard`, i.e. uncommitted working-tree state, which is why this is worth saying out loud rather than inheriting `tree` by silence. It is still `tree`: the subject is files in this repository's scripts/ directory, committed or not — not the machine and not a remote board. The untracked half cannot move the audit's number either, because both audit arms are fresh worktrees built from a commit and the audit refuses on a dirty tree, so neither arm has untracked files to count.

checks.name: census-why-matches-registry
checks.why: the census restates registry declarations in prose — "declares needs:board-read", "declares subjectKind:external" — and nothing compared the copy to its source. Two files hold the same fact, one generated and one hand-written, and every consumer reads the census sentence rather than the registry (#906)
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR, NOT A SNAPSHOT. The subject is the number of census reasons that QUOTE a registration — 8 today — and a floor pinned to 8 would fail the day a checker legitimately drops its channel. What must be caught is a run that verified NOTHING, and the floor catches only the TOTAL case: if eject-classify.mjs changed its wording entirely the claim set would fall to zero and this would refuse. A PARTIAL wording change is the likelier edit and the floor CANNOT see it — 8 claims becoming 7 stays above 1 and the unmatched row is silently unverified. That gap is closed by the checker instead, not by this floor: a `why` that begins "declares " and does not parse is a REFUSAL rather than a skip. The count below is provenance and moves whenever a check gains or loses `needs` or `subjectKind`.

checks.name: armed-pr-review-coverage
checks.why: auto-merge makes MERGE TIME unpredictable, so an armed pull request lands the moment its last check goes green — before a reader has finished, or after content was added that nobody read. #945 merged that way while the amendment fixing the paragraphs it falsified was still in flight AND THE ARMED SUBJECT WENT EMPTY (#1053): #945 produced both this gate and the practice that empties it — we stopped arming and merge one at a time by hand — so `armed` was zero continuously and every row short-circuited to UNARMED while the check reported ok, covering none of the four merges the night it was filed. The subject is now every MERGE CANDIDATE: armed, or green and not a draft and CLEAN-or-BEHIND, PLUS THE PULL REQUEST THIS RUN IS GATING, named by the event payload (#1074) -- because a subject defined over CHECK STATE and evaluated BY a check cannot contain the thing being gated, so every verdict this gate ever published about a pull request came from a run in which that pull request was invisible. BEHIND must be in, because under strict:true a branch is behind the moment anything else lands — measured at main 0eb40cb7, BEHIND 10 / DIRTY 3 / BLOCKED 1 / CLEAN 0 with all six greens BEHIND, so a CLEAN-keyed subject would be empty for the same reason the armed one is

checks.name: typescript-pin-justified
checks.why: dependabot.yml ignores typescript majors because tsup emits our .d.ts through a rollup-plugin-dts its published bundle froze at typescript@5.7.3, while the pnpm store key on that same directory says 6.0.3 — a resolution fact and a build fact that no lockfile query can compare. The pin therefore expires on an EVENT (tsup shipping a dist that no longer bakes an older TypeScript) which no date can observe, and it can go inert without anyone noticing: a person editing package.json is not Dependabot, and a second `ignore:` key in one mapping silently discards the first. This reads the installed bundle through fs rather than grep, because node_modules is gitignored and the shell's grep honours that, so a grep-based version would find nothing and pass vacuously forever (#1050, #1019)
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR, NOT A SNAPSHOT — the same reasoning as required-contexts. The subject is the .js files in every installed tsup dist, which is UPSTREAM'S choice of bundle layout: today it is 10, and a floor of 10 would be a scheduled failure the first time tsup merges or splits a chunk, reporting 'a green whose subject is under the floor' about a tree that is fine. What the floor must catch is examining NOTHING — a dist path that resolved to a directory with no .js files in it — and 1 does that completely. The load-bearing guard here is not the floor: a dist read with no `typescript@X.Y.Z` string in it REFUSES (exit 2) before any verdict, because that is the reading a broken search also produces. OBSERVED ON A REAL INSTALL, not on a borrowed one: the count comes from the audit's own full tree, cut at 481ba7ae and installed from this branch's lockfile (tsup@8.5.1 with postcss@8.5.28, which is main's resolution rather than the 8.5.26 in the checkout I first measured against). Re-measure by checking out that sha, installing, and running the checker: it prints its subject on the pass path.

checks.name: workflow-failures-surfaced
checks.why: three workflows were failing unseen at once and each was found by accident: mutation.yml red from 2026-08-30, ci-measurement.yml red from 2026-09-07 and unfiled, and the E2E live-transport job red for 40+ runs (#742). A workflow without a pull_request trigger cannot fail anywhere a person looks, and a job conditioned on push cannot either even when its workflow has one — a workflow-level check passes e2e.yml while its e2e-live-transport job is unreachable from any pull request, which is why this checks JOBS and not only workflows. It asserts VISIBILITY rather than enforcement, deliberately: enforce_admins is false here and PR #130 merged carrying check-runs total_count = 0, so a failing required check does not stop a merge and a gate claiming otherwise would claim something branch protection does not deliver (#1097, #1021, #742)
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR, NOT A SNAPSHOT, on the same reasoning as required-contexts and typescript-pin-justified. The subject is the workflow files in .github/workflows, which is 9 today and moves whenever anyone adds or retires a workflow — a floor of 9 would be a scheduled failure the first time one is deleted, reporting 'a green whose subject is under the floor' about a tree that is fine. What the floor must catch is examining NOTHING, and 1 does that completely. It is deliberately NOT the load-bearing guard: a .github/workflows that exists but holds no workflow files REFUSES (exit 2) before any verdict, because a pass over an empty directory asserts nothing and an absent directory is not a clean one

checks.name: no-regex-comment-stripping
checks.why: five instances of one defect were found in two days and every one was found because a person happened to notice — a regex cannot tell a comment from a URL, a glob or a path alias, and the class had four separate repairs and no detector (#1149)
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR, NOT A SNAPSHOT, and the distinction is the one #1131 records. The subject is the number of scripts PARSED — 228 today — and a floor at that number is a scheduled refusal: it fires the first time somebody legitimately deletes a script, and the deleter has done nothing wrong. What a floor must catch here is the subject collapsing to NOTHING, which is what a broken `git ls-files` or a bad filter produces, and 1 catches that completely. AND ITS floorObserved TAKES A sha WHERE `worktree-inventory` TAKES A source, which is not an inconsistency: this subject is a count of files in the tree, so a sha names a tree anyone can check out and re-measure. That check's subject is the worktree list of whatever machine runs it, which no sha can describe — so it records a source instead, and its own note says any snapshot floor there is a scheduled failure. Two entries, two forms, and the difference is a property of the subjects rather than of the authors.

checks.name: overrides-entail-declarations
checks.why: `pnpm.overrides` replaces a dependency's resolved version EVERYWHERE, including in workspaces whose own manifest declares a range, and pnpm does not warn when the override permits something that manifest rejects — the override is the thing it was told to obey. #1132 is the instance: an exact `react-dom` pin at 19.2.6 under a declared `^19.2.7`, surfacing only as ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH when Dependabot rewrote one copy of the overrides block and not the other. IT IS NOT SPECIFIC TO EXACT PINS: a FLOOR lower than a declared floor stops preventing a below-range resolution just as effectively, and two of this repo's eight overrides were in that state — correct only BY RESOLUTION, because pnpm picks the highest satisfying version and the registry offered one. Nothing asserted it. The subject is the LOWER bound; an override above every declared range is a real hazard in the other direction and is a declared non-subject, stated in the checker so the domain shrinks by a written rule rather than an unwritten one.
checks.floorNote: ZERO IS THE RIGHT FLOOR AND THE SUBJECT IS NARROWER THAN THE OVERRIDE COUNT. The subject is overrides a workspace manifest ALSO declares; six of the current eight are transitive-only and have no declared range to violate, so a tree whose overrides are all transitive legitimately examines zero. The vacuity that would matter is a checker that silently skips what it cannot parse, and that is guarded separately: the refused count is printed on EVERY run including zero, so a blind spot is a number rather than a possibility.

checks.name: every-pr-head-reached-ci

Every channel that would normally complain is quiet -- the push succeeded, the older runs still exist on shas that are no longer the head, and a page with no checks section reads as fine (#963). THE INSTANCE IS 538b742f on #1121, which was MERGEABLE at its push and got nothing while the next head 80 seconds later got six runs; #1086's 2a654bcc, the observation #1095 was filed on, turns out to be a dirty-at-push head and is explained rather than an instance. No cause survives for 538b742f, which is the argument for a gate reading the CONDITION rather than any mechanism
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR ON OPEN PULL REQUESTS, WHICH IS THE SUBJECT AND NOT THE FINDINGS. A count of heads with no CI is legitimately zero -- that is the state we want -- so a floor on findings would be the scheduled failure #768 records. What a floor must catch is the board listing answering with NOTHING, and 1 does that: this repository has not had zero open pull requests in its recorded history, so a zero here is the API rather than the board. The checker refuses separately on a null listing, and on a FULL page, because a floor can only see the empty end and truncation is the other one.

checks.name: nobody-reviews-their-own
checks.why: #1055 created AUTHORING-AGENT and nothing consumed it, so 'never assign someone their own pull request' was still enforced by a person remembering — the shape that reads as done while asserting nothing. The cost is measured: only jobordu is assignable here and every agent commits under it, so GitHub cannot express agent identity at all; in one dispatch round an ownership sweep reported 44 unowned issues where the real figure was 27, one issue was credited to the wrong agent, and another's subject was attributed to nobody. The join is on ROSTER IDENTITY rather than raw names because DEV3 and DEV3-lang are the same agent and both forms are live in different channels — declarations never carry the suffix, prose almost always does — so a string comparison misses exactly the self-review that spelled itself the other way. Two off-roster names are two unknowns and never a match, because null === null would accuse a reader on the strength of neither name being recognised (#1058, #1052, #915)
checks.floorNote: ZERO IS THE RIGHT FLOOR AND IT IS NOT A SHRUG. The subject is open pull requests carrying a LIVE reader report — 14 today, and a set that CAN legitimately be empty: a board between cycles, or one where every token has been withdrawn, examines nothing and no self-review is possible. A floor of 1 would fail the runner exactly where the checker deliberately passes, because the checker already announces the vacuity in its own words rather than reporting a green that reads as coverage: 'no open pull request carries a live reader report, so NOTHING was examined and this check asserts nothing about self-review'. So the guard against a vacuous pass lives in the OUTPUT, where a reader sees it, and the floor states the honest thing — that an empty domain is a real answer here. What would make a floor of 1 correct is a board that structurally always carries a token, and nothing guarantees that. AND IT DECLARES subjectKind:external WITH needs:pr-state, which the first registration omitted and the audit caught: run 1 classified it `moved`, 15 -> 14, because the LIVE BOARD changed between the two readings — a pull request gained a token in the eight minutes between them. That difference is not attributable to the eject and never could be. It is the worktree-inventory failure exactly: a subject read from outside the tree, compared across two readings taken minutes apart, reports motion that belongs to the world rather than to the ejection. The three sibling board-readers — armed-pr-review-coverage, every-branch-was-raised and pr-authorship-attributable — all declare both fields for the same reason.

unregistered.reason: it runs, but not from here — and it cannot. WHERE IT RUNS: .github/workflows/ci.yml, job `python:`, step "The approval vocabulary we offer is one the parser accepts (#669)" — which invokes `node scripts/assert-approval-vocabulary-agrees.selftest.mjs` and then the checker with `--python "$(command -v python)"`, after that job's `pip install -r requirements.txt` under `working-directory: apps/fastapi-backend`. That working directory is load-bearing: there is no requirements.txt at the repo root. Anchored on the job and step NAMES rather than line numbers, because rewriting the step's own comment in #771 moved the invocation by eight lines and stale line numbers in this field would be the same defect this entry documents. WHY IT CANNOT BE REGISTERED HERE: it asks an INSTALLED langchain what `interrupt_on={tool: True}` expands to, so it only runs where the backend requirements are installed, and `pnpm checks` runs in job `ci:`, which never installs them — registering it here would exit 2 on every run. NOT A CHANNEL, DELIBERATELY: a channel would convert that loud exit 2 into a quiet, correct, permanent NOT MEASURED, and run-checks.mjs makes exactly that argument about itself for `repo-settings` — a channel needs somewhere it is satisfied, and this one would have none. Exiting 2 when the interpreter cannot answer is the behaviour to keep. Permanent while `pnpm checks` runs in a job without the backend requirements; installing them there is the only thing that would change it, and it has not been judged worth a pip install on every node run.
requires run-specific arguments — it needs a base and a head, and the runner passes none.
consumes the runner's own output — it reads .checks-run.json, which run-checks WRITES. A check registered here would read a record of a run that had not finished.

not a node script — run-checks spawns `process.execPath <script>` (run-checks.mjs:484), so this would run as `node x.sh`. AND it requires run-specific arguments (`--label`, `--forbid-module`, positional subjects; ci.yml:838), so a port to .mjs would not admit it either. Two independent reasons.

its subject is an install that has not happened yet. It runs at ci.yml:89, BEFORE `pnpm install` at :92, deliberately; `pnpm checks` is at :790. A registered copy would run where the install has necessarily already succeeded, so it could never fail — a vacuous entry. The argument is ci.yml:82's, which predates this change.

requires run-specific arguments — `--record <file>` or `--verify <file> --retained a,b,c`. Found by RUNNING it, not by reading: clause 2 has no fixed vocabulary, and a scan for --base/--head/--at does not see --record/--verify.

not a checker — it is `pnpm format`, the developer command that REWRITES the tree. A checker that writes would be a control running downstream of its own effect. CI runs `pnpm test:format` (its proof, by mutation) but never `pnpm format`, and that asymmetry is deliberate: the gate that asserts formatting is `formatted` in this file, which reads and does not write. Its proof running is not it running.

not a checker — it is `pnpm freeze:all`, the maintainer command that SETTLES the frozen artifacts other checkers compare against. It writes the baseline; asserting against a baseline you just wrote is the shape a control must not have. Its proof runs in CI; the command is run by hand before committing a moved number.

not a checker — it MEASURES and does not assert, and its own header opens by saying so. It has no failing verdict to give: it partitions flake occurrences for a human to read, and is imported by verdict-streak.mjs. Registering it would demand a floor and a subject for a number that is an observation rather than a claim.

not a checker — its header states the rule directly: "Property measured, not asserted". It reports how long a red survives on a push-only job. Imported by verdict-streak.mjs. NOTE, and this is the only one of the six where it is true: its own proof is invoked by no workflow either, so nothing exercises it in CI at all. That is worth its own issue rather than a silent line here.

not a checker — it is a shared harness, imported as a module rather than run as a program. Nothing invokes it as a step and nothing should. It is in this population only because it has a proof of its own, which is correct: a harness that silently stopped mutating would make every proof that uses it vacuous. THAT MUCH IS PERMANENT AND IS WHY THE ENTRY STAYS. THE ADOPTION CLAUSE WAS WRITTEN IN THE PRESENT TENSE ABOUT A STATE THAT NEVER ARRIVED (#1107). It read "the shared harness that mutation-based PROOFS import, so it executes whenever they do". Measured on 2026-09-08 at origin/main: ONE file imports it, its own selftest — against a positive control finding six importers of scripts/lib/eject-classify.mjs with the same query form, so the zero-adopters reading is a real zero rather than a broken query. Re-take it with `git grep -l mutation-proof origin/main -- 'scripts/*.mjs'`. AND THE FALSE SENTENCE IS THE DEMONSTRATED CAUSE OF A FIFTH REIMPLEMENTATION: it reads as ALREADY IN USE to someone deciding whether to go looking, so they do not look — which is the same failure the harness was extracted to end, arriving through its own documentation. .github/workflows/ci.yml:882 has said the honest thing all along — the family is CONVERGING on it — and two records of one fact, one aspirational and one indicative, is why only the indicative one misled. WHAT WOULD MAKE THE CLAUSE TRUE, which is not the same as retiring this entry: the next mutation-based proof written should import this rather than open-coding a fifth mechanism, and the clause becomes accurate at the first such importer. Migrating the existing proofs is a separate and larger question that needs a proposal with a cost, not a drive-by.

not a checker — a helper imported by census.mjs and classify.mjs to write a generated JSON artifact in the shape the format gate expects. Executed as a module by its importers, never invoked as a step.

NOT A CHECKER — a diagnostic census over CI history, and it cannot run from the gate: it calls the GitHub API for a run listing and then one job log per run, so registering it would make every check on every PR depend on network reachability and a token, and would spend a log fetch per run to answer a question nobody asks per commit. WHERE IT RUNS: on demand, by whoever is investigating a flake, as `node scripts/flake-census.mjs --since <ISO>`. ITS PARSER IS PURE AND IS PROVEN: scripts/flake-census.selftest.mjs drives readFlakeReport over fixtures with no network at all, and ci.yml runs it. Permanent while the census reads the API; nothing about it would become gate-shaped by a change to this repo.

NOT A CHECKER — a measurement tool, and registering it would put a five-minute run on every PR. WHERE IT RUNS: `pnpm eject-audit` (package.json), on demand, by whoever adds or changes a checker — because scripts/assert-eject-subjects-classified.mjs is the registered gate that tells them to. WHY IT CANNOT BE REGISTERED: measured, not estimated — it runs the full check suite TWICE, 193s on the full tree and 191s on an ejected one, plus a 2s eject, a 5s install and a ~25s build of each. That is the 'minutes' branch of #755's split: the gate is cheap and total and runs per PR; this produces the entries the gate checks for. Registering it would buy one measurement of a small changing subset at the cost of measuring all 48 on every PR. NOT A CHANNEL, DELIBERATELY: a channel would turn a loud 'the census is stale' into a quiet permanent NOT MEASURED, and a channel needs somewhere it is satisfied — this one would have none, because there is no CI job that should spend ten minutes on it. Permanent while the audit costs minutes; if the check suite ever became seconds this could be registered like anything else, and that is the only thing that would change it.

NOT A CHECKER — the PRODUCER for scripts/eject-subject-audit.mjs, and unregistered for the same measured reason that one is: it runs the full check suite TWICE and additionally ejects, installs and builds a second worktree, so ~7-8 minutes on every PR to measure a subset that changes only when someone registers a checker. WHERE IT RUNS: `pnpm eject-audit`, on demand, by whoever the registered gate scripts/assert-eject-subjects-classified.mjs has just told to run it. WHY IT EXISTS AT ALL (#819): that gate's remediation named `pnpm eject-audit`, and `pnpm eject-audit` was wired straight to the CONSUMER, which refuses without four arguments no workflow supplied and no example anywhere in the tree demonstrated. The instruction could not be followed, and the first person to hit it correctly stopped rather than guess — guessing would have produced the plausible-but-wrong census the audit's own header warns about. ITS PROOF IS CHEAP AND IS NOT THIS: scripts/eject-audit-run.selftest.mjs covers every decision made before anything expensive runs, plus the record check made after, which is the set that decides whether a bad census can be written. Permanent while the audit costs minutes — the same condition that governs the consumer, and the only thing that would change it.
